transcript.text: From what you have described, the most likely cause is that zone's element or its control. Many hobs have a key / child lock (often a key or padlock symbol) that stops the zones coming on — the manual shows which button to hold. Was the lock on (and is it off now), or was there no lock on?
no I don't think the lock was on, the other rings work fine. Only the back right one won't heat up
Now try switching a zone on. Is it working now, or still not?
I haven't changed anything yet, I only just told you the lock wasn't on. Do you want me to try switching the back right one on? It's still not heating if so, the number shows but no glow

No need to keep trying it for now. You've already told us it shows a number but doesn't glow, which is enough to go on, so leave it switched off while you do the next check. Check the hob's isolator switch (often a large switch on the wall or in a cupboard) is on, and look at the fuse box for a breaker that has switched off. If a breaker keeps tripping, don't keep resetting it. Was the isolator or a breaker off (and is it sorted), or were they all on?
The other three rings work so the power must be getting to the hob. I haven't found any tripped breaker, no. Not sure where the isolator switch is though, I'll have a look.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
